newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bank profit growth slows.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank profit growth slows.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest bank, on Thursday reported a nine percent rise in group net income in the first nine months of 1996, marking a slowdown from 15 percent growth in the first half of the year.

Group net profit rose to 1.5 billion marks ($985 million) from 1.4 billion ($921 million) while operating profit jumped 25.8 percent to 3.49 billion ($2.3 billion), the bank said in its interim report. The results were broadly in line with expectations.

Analysts said the slowdown was caused by an acceleration in administration costs during the third quarter as Deutsche continued to throw money at its expanding investment bank business, concentrated at London unit Morgan Grenfell.

Net earnings were also restrained by a sharp rise in taxes to 1.5 billion marks ($987 million) from 1 billion marks ($658 million) and by the cost of bailing out Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), hit by irregularities at three unit trusts.

But Deutsche's profit growth was buoyant nonetheless, driven by a 46.6 percent surge in trading income to 2.1 billion marks ($1.4 billion) as financial markets continued to rise. That level exceeded its entire 1995 trading profit of 2.0 billion marks ($1.3 billion).
